quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What are the penalties for fleeing from police to avoid arrest?

options.text: The driver can be charged with a misdemeanor or felony.
The driver's license can be revoked.

questions.explanation: Fleeing from police is itself a crime. If you flee from a misdemeanor charge, it is a misdemeanor. If you flee from a felony charge, it is a felony. In both cases, your license can be revoked.

questions.question: What should you do when you encounter an aggressive driver?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Make sure they know you disapprove of their driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If another driver is driving dangerously near you, stay calm. Slow down and let them pass. Do not look at them or make hand gestures. Try to put distance between you and them.

questions.question: Using a handheld phone while driving is a secondary offense when you use it to:

options.text: Read, type, or send written messages.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read, type, or send written messages.
questions.explanation: Using a handheld phone to read, type, or send messages while driving is a secondary offense. The fine is between $200 and $500.

questions.question: When you see angry drivers around you, what should you do?

options.text: Don't make eye contact with them.

questions.explanation: When drivers are angry, keep your distance from them. Avoid eye contact and hand gestures. Slow down, move to another lane, or do whatever you can safely do to stay away from them.

questions.question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?

options.text: It should be snug across your hip bones and lower belly.
It should be hidden under the seat.
It should stop the seat belt warning light from turning on.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be snug across your hip bones and lower belly.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should sit snugly across your hip bones and lower belly. The shoulder belt should fit comfortably so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you?

options.text: Speed up to get away from it.
Stop immediately and block its path.
Do everything you can to clear the road for it.
Signal to it when it is safe to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do everything you can to clear the road for it.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near, give it a clear path. If it is safe, pull to the side of the road to let it pass.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle is stopped on the road with flashing lights, what must you do?

options.text: Move into another lane, at least one lane away from the stopped vehicle if possible.
Pull onto the left shoulder and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane, at least one lane away from the stopped vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, move into a lane that is at least one lane away if you can do so safely. If you cannot change lanes safely, slow down and pass it carefully.

questions.question: What should you do if you encounter an aggressive driver?
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to get out of an aggressive driver's way. Never try to compete with other drivers. Follow the rules and respect all road users.

questions.question: Is it a violation to not use a child safety seat for children under age six?
questions.explanation: Children under age six must be in a federally-approved child safety seat. Not using one is a violation that costs $25 (plus court costs) and adds one point to your driving record.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle using sirens and flashing lights approaches, should you pull to the right and wait for it to pass?
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights and sirens approaches, pull to the right side of the road right away and let it pass.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol with drugs can:
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can increase the effects of both. It is unsafe to drive after consuming alcohol or drugs. It is even more dangerous to drive after mixing them.

questions.question: Lack of sleep affects your driving ability the same way as:
questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol have similar effects on driving ability. Being awake for 18 hours impairs driving about as much as a 0.05 percent blood alcohol level. Being awake for 24 hours has the same effect as a 0.10 percent blood alcohol level.

questions.question: Barricades, vertical panels, drums, and cones are used to guide drivers safely through work zones.
questions.explanation: Barricades, vertical panels, drums, and cones guide drivers safely through work zones. Be careful when driving through work zones.

questions.question: This symbol is used for:
questions.explanation: A reflective orange triangle on the rear of a vehicle warns that it moves slowly. You may see this on roadwork equipment, farm vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons. It looks orange during the day and red at night.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left at an intersection, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Once the intersection is clear and traffic signals allow, you can complete the turn.

questions.question: Distracted driving can be caused by:

options.text: Talking or texting on a phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.

questions.explanation: Drivers must make 200 decisions for every mile driven. Full focus on driving is critical. Any extra task creates a dangerous distraction.

questions.question: The maximum posted speed limit should only be driven:
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest legal speed under ideal conditions. Drive at the same speed as other traffic, up to the limit. All drivers must drive safely at all times.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. They are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a curve in the road ahead.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop at the first rest stop or service area. Take a nap, stretch, or switch drivers. Caffeine pills and energy drinks are not a replacement for rest and can make driving more dangerous.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, what helps ensure safe driving?

options.text: Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: Arrange a ride home with a sober friend. Drinking coffee or taking a cold shower does not reduce blood alcohol or its effects. It takes about one hour for the body to eliminate one drink of alcohol.

questions.question: You should slow down:

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, at intersections and railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp or blind curves, where there are pedestrians or hazards, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: The most common mistake when backing up is not looking both ways behind the car.
questions.explanation: The most common mistake when backing up is not looking both ways behind the car. Mirrors do not show everything. Turn your body and head to the right and look through the rear window to see as much as possible.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Focus only on the middle of the road.
Watch beside, ahead, and behind the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch beside, ahead, and behind the car.
questions.explanation: A driver should watch beside, ahead, and behind the car. Good drivers know what is happening all around their vehicle.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the right lane ends ahead.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. If a solid yellow line is next to a broken yellow line, drivers on the solid line side cannot pass. Sometimes both lines are solid, which means no one can pass in either direction.
